We entered the building, and there were seats for students there, two or three in one row and three or four in the other row, and that's where Cuk and Genov were sitting as we walked in.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What was happening when you walked in?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Those two were already being beaten by men who were there. It was Genov and Cuk who were being beaten. I remember that Cuk had to hit his head against a wall. The two of us sat in the back seat, and I was facing the middle of the room. Genov was sitting next to me, and Cuk was in front later on when they picked them up -- when they picked him up from the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: The men who were there, as you say, what were these men wearing, the men who were beating Cuk and -- Cuk?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms, some of them, and others in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did they have weapons?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, they did have weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Were these soldiers asking any questions of Genov and Cuk?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: They were asking them who they were, what they did. I remember that Genov said that he worked in Electrokosovo. He did not mention the army. He probably knew what would happen to him if he did. Cuk kept saying that he was a refugee, that he had nothing to do with anything, that his field of work was construction and things like that. Later on, they asked me and Ivan, too, what we were and who we were. We said that we were refugees, that we were on our way to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Before you get there, did you personally speak to Genov at any time in this classroom?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Not then, no. Not by then. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: When did you speak with Genov? Did you speak with him at any time while you were in this school building that you've described?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Only once, when he offered me his wallet, and I said, "I can't."

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Why did he offer you his wallet?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Later on, I realised why. I mean, I realised why when his wallet dropped out of his pocket. In his wallet, he had his military ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What happened after his wallet fell out of his pocket?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: They were beating him, and that's how his wallet fell out. Then they picked it up. They opened it, and they realised who he was, and that was the end of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Where were Genov and Cuk being beaten? Was it -- was it in the classroom or was it outside of the classroom where you were?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Before they found that wallet that belonged to Cuk or -- I'm sorry, to Genov, they beat them there, and they also took them out of that room. My Ivan cried terribly. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could you see Genov and Cuk being beaten?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. We just heard them moaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What about while they were in the classroom? Did you see them being beaten there?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. They beat Genov when they saw that military ID. Then this man who had asked for our documents on the bus literally jumped on him and started beating him on the legs and on the chest. He was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What did they use to beat Genov? Did they use their fists or did they kick him? How did they beat him?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: They kicked him. They hit him with their hands and fists, and at one moment even with a rifle butt.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: How many soldiers participated in beating them?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: It was only that one soldier who was beating them there. As for the other place, I don't know. Usually it was just one person who was doing the beating, not two.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: How many soldiers did you see while you were in the classroom, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: There were more than five of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: How long did these beatings last?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I could not say exactly. At any rate, until it got dark, because they were waiting for nightfall in order for us to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What was the condition of Genov and Cuk by the time this beating was over?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Genov was in pain. At one moment, he was unconscious. Cuk was just beaten up. He had bruises on his head. But it was Genov who was really the victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may be an appropriate time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn now and resume at ten past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Actually, this would be -- could we go into private session for a few questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, before the break you told us that they had been waiting for nightfall before taking you from this classroom, I believe. What happened after the beatings of Cuk and Genov ended? Did you leave the school building?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. We went to a van, if I can call it that. First they brought Cuk and Genov in. They were tied. Ivan and I were not tied. We boarded the van after they did. They put plastic bags on their heads, and they gave us blindfolds, some kind of bands. Then we set off for this other location.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Who was in the kombi besides yourself and your son and Genov and Cuk?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: A driver and one or two men. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Were these men armed?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Were did these men take you?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: They took us to a house on a farm, I think. I don't know where this was. I only learned about it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let me ask you, what happened when you arrive at your destination?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: They entered the yard, then. There was a big gate there. We stood in front of the door of a house, and they took the two of them in and they took the two of us in, Ivan and me, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did they remove your blindfold?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. It was night-time. You couldn't see anything in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You said, "They took the two of us in." Into where?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: The ground floor of that house. First through a small kitchen or something like that, and then to the left where there was a sort of dining-room. There were some things that I wouldn't really call sofas. There was something like sponge-like foam bedding.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You said that you couldn't see anything in the yard because it was night-time. Could you see inside this room or this place you were taken?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw this small room and the place where we were sitting because the light was on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: With the assistance of Mr. Younis, I'd like to show the witness part of Prosecution Exhibit P5, which will appear on his screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you see that? Do you see an image on your screen, sir?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Younis, if you could go in the ground floor of the building labelled A1. Continue. And if you could pan around slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, can you recognise this room?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the room that we were brought to after the school, except that there wasn't anything like a couch there. There were only these foam mattresses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: If I could ask Mr. Younis to pan around to the left again. Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Where were these foam mattresses?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: On the floor by the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I think we can turn off Sanction now for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, when you arrived in this room, did you see any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw a few men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember the name or nickname of any of those soldiers that you saw?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I do not remember any names or nicknames. I found out about one particular name later on, and I remembered that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Which name was that?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Shala.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Was Shala present in this room when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I could not say with any degree of certainty. There were a lot of people there, and I did not know anyone at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What was happening in this room when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: The mistreatment of Genov started again. Cuk not that much, but Genov was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember who was beating Genov?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: There was a young man, sort of good looking, well-built. He's the one who beat him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember how tall, approximately, this young man was?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I think he was about as tall as I am or perhaps a bit shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember the colour of his hair?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: He had darker hair, and he also wore a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did this person ever say anything to you about his education or background?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Afterwards, he told me that he had studied at the university, that he attended the PE school, physical education, and that he also knew martial arts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can you describe how he beat Genov?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: With his hands and feet, and he jumped on him, all of that. I don't remember all the details. He was really beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did this soldier say anything while he was beating Genov?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: More or less how many people had the sergeant killed, things like that. And that was invariably followed by beatings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: At the beginning of your testimony, I asked you about statements that you'd given previously to the ICTY and to another organisation, the humanitarian law centre. Do you remember that? Do you remember those questions of mine?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember if in those other statements you also described this person that you've now told us was beating Stamen Genov?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you think you described him essentially the way you've described him just now?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, how many soldiers altogether were in the room, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: There were other soldiers there, but I can't remember the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms. Some were all in black. Some wore civilian clothing. Their attire was mixed for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember if any of them had weapons?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, they did have weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did any of these other soldiers also beat Genov?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Why did the soldiers appear to target Genov and not to beat you or Cuk or your son?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I think it was because he was a military man.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could you explain why would him being a military man lead the soldiers to target him?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would make an observation there's been a lack of foundation that the opinion being asked for is within this particular witness's purview.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just asking, he was there, based on his impressions, but if you would like me to move on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, at any time during the beating of Genov, were you and your son taken out of the room?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What was the last thing that you remember happening in this room?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: One of the soldiers said that a little girl in Djakovica had just been raped. Then the man who was beating him took a knife out and made a movement toward his genitals. Then they took Ivan and me out in front of the house, and I heard Genov pleading with him, saying, "Please don't. I never killed anyone." He was saying things to defend himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you know if the soldier did anything to Genov with the knife that he was threatening him with?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: No, you don't know, or no, he didn't do anything to Genov with that knife?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, he didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: How long did this beating of Stamen Genov last altogether? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Soon after that, they transferred us to another room.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What time was it approximately when they transferred you to another room?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What was Stamen Genov's condition when they took you to another room?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very serious condition. They practically had to carry him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You say that they transferred you to another room. Describe how that happened, please.

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact details, but at any rate, after the incident with the knife, soon after that, we all went to the basement. First the two of them, and then they wondered what they'd do with us, and then they said that we should be taken to the basement too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember who said that you should be taken to the basement too?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I don't know who said that. At any rate, I do know that it had been said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I'd like you to briefly describe the basement to which you were taken.

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: It was somewhere in the middle of the yard of that property. There was a small window and a door. After the door opened, there was a small step, and then you'd enter the room. I don't know the exact dimensions. About three by five or six metres. I can't say exactly. They took us in there. Some people were already there. They had been there for quite awhile already.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Please tell us who was already there when you arrived.

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: When we arrived, of course we didn't manage to see everything immediately, but we realised that there was a total of 13 people in that basement, including ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can you tell me what you remember about those 13 people? Who were they?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Three ethnic Albanians were detained there, six ethnic Serbs, and the four of us, the four newcomers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can you give me any description of the three ethnic Albanians?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I couldn't really describe them, because I practically didn't see them at all. They slept all the time. Nobody ever touched them. And after all, it was dark in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Would you be able to estimate how old they were?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What about the six ethnic Serbs that were there when you arrived? Please tell me what you know about them.

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: There was a young man by the name of Zeljko. I don't know his last name. He had been wounded in his leg. There was an elderly gentleman. He was sick. He had diabetes, and right before these events, he had undergone eye surgery. There were the Krstic brothers. I don't know the names of the other people there. I think that one of them was called Slobodan. I remember that because my father's name is Slobodan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you a few questions about what you've just told us. You mentioned the Krstic brothers. Do you know where they were from?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: I think they were from Suva Reka. They were stopped as they were driving in their civilian Golf, as they told me at that time. They were intercepted. Their car was taken away, and they were taken to the basement. I don't know how they got there, but that's where they ended up, in that basement. As for another gentleman, he had been abducted from a bus. We learned from them that they had already been there for seven days by the time we arrived. The three Albanians had been there even longer. Now, I don't know whether that is accurate or not. That's what we heard from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: To be clear, did you speak with these other men that were in the basement with you?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Not much. They told us only those things. They knew that we would be released. I don't know how they found that out. They probably talked to somebody up there. We didn't. But they consoled us saying that we would be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Were the prisoners in the basement permitted to speak to one another?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: We mostly whispered, and only when it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned an older man who seemed to be sick. What more can you tell me about him?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Only that he had diabetes and an eye injury which had caused him to undergo surgery. I don't remember what else, what to say, what other characteristics he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you ever learn how he had arrived in the camp -- or in the basement. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. No. Perhaps -- I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Later, did you ever meet with anyone from this man's family? Can you remember anything like that?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. A man approached me, showed me a photograph and asked me if I had seen that man. I said yes but that I didn't know what had happened to him. It was in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And when did that happen, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: It was a day or two -- because I was in Pristina for two days. I arrived in the evening and stayed in Pristina for another day. I stayed with a lady who was the secretary of the Red Cross organisation for Kosovo. It must have been in the Red Cross reception centre where I went to see a doctor, because I was in a very bad shape psychologically. So it must have happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: So it was, just to be clear, after you'd left this place, after you were released?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you earlier about meeting with a Tribunal investigator in January 2003. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember if that investigator showed you any photographs of people that you recognised as being in the basement with you?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did he also show you some photographs of people that you did not recognise?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could go into private session. I'd like to show him some photographs, some of which are public but a few or not. So if we could just go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Sir, can you remember how you and the other prisoners you've described were arranged in the basement, where you sat? Can you remember that today?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember. I think I actually made a drawing in my statement indicating where the detainees were in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: At this time I'd like to show the witness, and we can do this on Sanction, this is public, the ERN for the record is U0032209. If it makes things any easier, we'll also give the witness a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. I drew this. That was how the people were situated in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember making -- do you remember drawing this at your interview with a Tribunal investigator in January 2003?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. That's when I made this drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And as you look at it today, does it appear to be accurate?

utterances.speaker: VOJKO BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Because this sick man, I remember now, he lay there just next to the window, and the Krstic brothers were right next to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this be given the next Prosecution Exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Prosecution Exhibit P78.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And we're finished with that document now. Your Honour, this is probably a good time to break. I could go on for five more minutes if you want me to. I'm in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we'll take your suggestion. Thank you, Mr. Black, and we'll adjourn for the night. Mr. Bakrac, we're going to adjourn for the evening now, and continue tomorrow in the afternoon. You will be advised precisely when to be here, and we'll resume again and hear the balance of your evidence. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
